core_obligations: Identify the limit term (proof lines 6422-6448): the objects of interest are bigraded by the construction of the spectral sequence, so if the displayed intersections of the cycle objects and unions of the boundary objects exist, then the cycle and boundary objects of the limit exist with those bigraded parts, by an elementary argument on unions and intersections of bigraded objects; consequently the limit term is the displayed quotient in each bidegree.

Compare with the cohomology (proof lines 6448-6476): with the total degree written as the sum of the two bidegrees, the kernel of the differential intersected with one filtration step is contained in the intersection defining the top of the limit term, and the union defining its bottom is contained in the image of the differential intersected with the same filtration step; hence a subquotient of the limit term is the displayed quotient, which by the identification of the graded pieces of the cohomology gives the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Show that the limit cycle and boundary objects exist bidegree by bidegree.
Compute the limit term as the displayed quotient.
Compare with the graded pieces of the cohomology through the two displayed inclusions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a filtered complex whose limit cycle and boundary objects exist in each bidegree, the limit term of the spectral sequence exists with the expected bigraded parts and the graded pieces of the cohomology are subquotients of it (statement lines 6404-6417). The proof (proof lines 6418-6476) identifies the bigraded pieces of the limit cycle and boundary objects, computes the limit term as an explicit quotient, and compares it with the graded cohomology through two inclusions. H2: a complete verification whose displayed inclusions are checkable by the reader.
